prompt: Implement run_loop(jobs, initial_tasks, budget) in Python using only the standard library. This is a deterministic callback-queue model of the HTML 0cd32204 event-loop checkpoint rule, not a browser implementation. There is one FIFO ordinary-task source and one FIFO microtask queue; cross-source browser scheduling, rendering, timers, Promise resolution, and exceptions are outside this model. jobs is a dict mapping 0–20 unique nonempty string IDs to lists of 0–20 instructions. Each instruction is an exact two-element list [op, arg], where op is 'emit', 'micro', or 'task'; emit's arg is any string to append to the log, and the other args are existing job IDs to append to the corresponding queue. initial_tasks is a list of 0–20 existing job IDs, with repetitions allowed; the microtask queue starts empty. budget is an int (not bool) from 0 to 1000 counting completed callbacks. A callback executes all of its instructions in order without interruption. At each callback boundary choose the oldest microtask whenever that queue is nonempty, otherwise choose the oldest ordinary task. In particular, drain newly added microtasks before selecting another ordinary task; cyclic enqueueing is allowed and is bounded by budget. Stop when both queues are empty or budget callbacks have run, without discarding queued work. Return an exact dict with keys 'trace', 'log', 'tasks', 'microtasks', and 'status': trace is a list of two-element lists [kind, job_id] in callback execution order (kind is 'task' or 'micro'); log is the list of emitted strings; tasks and microtasks are the remaining FIFO job-ID lists; status is 'idle' if both queues are empty, otherwise 'budget'. If queues become empty on the last allowed callback, status is idle. Inputs contain only these valid shapes and values; invalid-input handling is not required. Do not mutate any input or retain state between calls. Return only built-in dict/list/str values of the stated shapes.

Implement cancellation_chain(tasks, requests), a pure analyzer of one fixed CPython 3.14.7 delegated-cancellation scenario. tasks is a ROOT-to-LEAF list of 1–8 exact records {id:str, suppress:bool, value:int}. IDs are unique, case-sensitive ASCII matching [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}. value lies in [-100,100]; requests is an integer from 0 to 5; integers exclude bool. Initially every Task has cancelling()==0 and no pending cancellation. Every Task has already entered its handler and is suspended awaiting the next Task in this chain; the leaf awaits a plain pending built-in asyncio Future. Each body normally returns its awaited result unchanged. If that body RECEIVES CancelledError, suppress=False propagates it; suppress=True returns that Task's supplied value. Make all requests calls to root.cancel BEFORE ANY Task step or wakeup runs, then drive the finite chain to quiescence. Every call is accepted while all Tasks remain pending, and delegation increments cancelling() on every Task for each request. The plain leaf Future is cancelled by the first request. Delivery then starts at the leaf and propagates upward only through children that finish cancelled: once a child catches cancellation and returns normally, ancestors receive its normal value rather than an injected cancellation, even though their cancelling counts stay positive. Several requests in this pre-wakeup batch do not create several deliveries through a handler. With 0 requests, every Task and the leaf Future remain pending. No uncancel, shield, external completion, other cancellation or exception, cleanup await, new task, or blocking work occurs; every activated handler returns or propagates in finite steps and the loop is driven. Return exactly {cancel_results:[bool,...], leaf_future_cancelled:bool, tasks:[{id:str, state:'pending'|'returned'|'cancelled', cancelling:int, received_cancel:bool, value:int_or_None},...in_ROOT_to_LEAF_order]}. cancel_results contains one True for each accepted request. leaf_future_cancelled describes the plain Future independently of whether the leaf Task suppresses its exception. Returned tasks carry their integer result; pending and cancelled tasks carry None. A suppressing ancestor uses its own configured value only if its handler actually receives cancellation. All containers and scalar types are exact built-in dict/list/str/int/bool/None values, with the stated ordering. Do not mutate inputs or retain state across calls. No outside-domain validation is required. Use only the standard library, with no network or actual async execution. This is a bounded delegation/handler component, not a full runtime, timing, cleanup, or scheduling simulator.

Implement queue_accounting(capacity, events), a pure CPython 3.14.7 Queue state/accounting model, not an async scheduler. capacity is an integer, excluding bool, in [-2,8]; capacity<=0 means unbounded. events contains at most 100 exact records of these forms: {op:'put',item:ID}, {op:'get'}, {op:'task_done'}, {op:'join'}, or {op:'shutdown',immediate:bool}. Item IDs are case-sensitive ASCII strings matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,16}; duplicate item values are allowed. Start with queue=[], unfinished=0, shutdown=False. put models put_nowait: if shut down, report shutdown before checking fullness; otherwise a full positive-capacity queue reports full without mutation, and a successful put appends the item, increments unfinished and reports accepted. get models get_nowait: if nonempty, remove and return the FIFO item WITHOUT decrementing unfinished, even after graceful shutdown; if empty, report shutdown when closed, otherwise empty. task_done decrements unfinished iff it is positive and reports acknowledged; otherwise report underflow with no mutation. Early acknowledgments are accepted because the actual method does not verify get/processing history. join is only a point query of whether a NEW awaited join would return immediately: report ready iff unfinished==0, otherwise waiting; it creates no persistent waiter. shutdown always closes the queue and reports closed. immediate=False preserves queue and count; immediate=True drains Q queued entries and sets unfinished=max(unfinished-Q,0). Repeated shutdown never reopens the queue, and graceful-to-immediate escalation may drain remaining items. Return a list of independent snapshots, one AFTER each event, with exact keys {op,status,value,queue,unfinished,shutdown}; return [] for empty events. value is the item only for successful get, otherwise None. The status choices are put: accepted/full/shutdown; get: item/empty/shutdown; task_done: acknowledged/underflow; join: ready/waiting; shutdown: closed. queue is the current FIFO list; unfinished is an int; shutdown is bool. These status outcomes model the APIs rather than raising their corresponding full/empty/underflow exceptions. All input/output containers and scalars are exact built-in dict/list/str/int/bool/None values. Do not mutate inputs or retain state across calls. Only the listed valid schemas are tested; modeled full/empty/underflow outcomes are in-domain. Use only the standard library, without real asynchronous execution or network.

Implement channel_ownership(capacity, owners, initial_queue, events), a bounded SERIAL ownership/admission ledger for Tokio 1.53.0 send/reserve effects, not its scheduler or internal semaphore-wakeup implementation. capacity is an int from 1 to 4, excluding bool. owners maps 0–4 live owner IDs to lists of owned opaque message IDs; initial_queue is FIFO and has length<=capacity. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII strings matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,16}. Message identities are globally unique across all initial owner lists and the queue, with at most 24 total. Owner, operation and message names occupy separate namespaces. There are at most 80 events and 24 operation IDs; operation IDs are fresh when created and are never reused. Exact event forms and effects: {op:'send',id,owner,value} moves a caller-owned value into a new incomplete send operation; {op:'reserve',id,owner} creates an incomplete capacity reservation without moving a message; {op:'send_ready',id} consumes an incomplete send and enqueues its value; {op:'reserve_ready',id} changes an incomplete reserve into an owned permit; {op:'cancel',id} applies only to an incomplete send or reserve, dropping the send's owned value but leaving caller values untouched for reserve; {op:'permit_send',id,value} moves the permit owner's value into the queue and consumes the permit; {op:'permit_drop',id} consumes a permit and releases its capacity; {op:'receive'} removes the nonempty queue's FIFO head into a received list; {op:'owner_drop',owner} drops all that live owner's caller-owned values and incomplete-send values, cancels its incomplete reservations, releases its permits, and removes that owner. Already-enqueued or received values are unaffected by owner drop. send_ready and reserve_ready require one modeled free slot; permit_send exchanges a held slot for a queued value. All referenced owners/operations/messages exist in the required ownership and operation-kind state; receive requires a nonempty queue, and owner_drop requires a live owner. Inputs supply valid successful API-outcome stages: no intermediate semaphore grants, wait-queue fairness, first-poll timing or partially progressed internal states are modeled, and the ledger does not predict when an incomplete operation becomes ready. A receiver and an external sender stay alive and open throughout. Each active operation is exactly {kind:'send'|'reserve'|'permit',owner:ID,value:messageID_or_None}; value is a message only for send and None otherwise. Initially operations, dropped and received are empty. Return a list of independent snapshots AFTER every event, or [] for empty events. Each snapshot has exact keys {op,queue,owners,operations,dropped,received,free}. owners maps live owner IDs to sorted message lists; operations maps active operation IDs to the stated records; dropped is sorted. Sorting is ordinary case-sensitive Python string order; dict key order does not matter. queue and received retain FIFO/receipt order. free=capacity-len(queue)-number_of_live_permits is the abstract ledger's unused capacity, not a measured runtime internal statistic. Every original message stays in exactly one location: caller ownership, incomplete send, queue, received, or dropped. Inputs must remain unchanged and calls independent; all containers and scalars are exact built-in dict/list/str/int/None values. No invalid-input validation is required. Use only the standard library, with no real Tokio execution, threads or network.

Implement pool_completion(capacity, running, queued, dependencies), a pure analyzer of a declared closed fixed-capacity thread-pool model. capacity is an integer from 1 to 4, never bool. There are 0–12 unique unfinished jobs total, with case-sensitive ASCII IDs matching [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}. running lists the initially executing jobs and has length at most capacity; queued is a disjoint FIFO list of all remaining jobs. dependencies maps exactly ALL job IDs to lists of distinct IDs in that same set. Queued jobs are finite independent LEAF work and must have empty dependency lists. Initially running jobs are at synchronous result barriers requiring ALL listed dependencies to finish; cycles and self-waits are permitted as closed mathematical inputs. No job is initially completed. There are no new jobs, timeouts, cancellations, failures, external completions, preemption, extra workers, or callback work. A running job whose dependencies are all completed can finish in finite time, publish its result and release its worker. Apply this canonical reduction repeatedly: first complete the lexicographically smallest currently completable RUNNING job; if none can finish and a worker slot is free, start the FIFO queued head; otherwise stop. Starting consumes one worker slot even before the new job completes. A just-started queued leaf is considered for completion on the next iteration. Completion takes priority over another start even when a slot is free. Return exactly {started:[newly_started_queued_ids], completed:[completion_order], running:[remaining_running_ids_sorted], queued:[remaining_FIFO_ids], deadlocked:bool}. Initially running jobs are not newly started entries. deadlocked is true iff jobs remain at the terminal state where no transition is possible; residuals include downstream waiters and are not a minimal cycle-membership set. An empty graph returns empty lists and false. Comparisons use ordinary case-sensitive Python lexical ordering. All containers and scalar types are exact built-in dict/list/str/int/bool values. Do not mutate inputs or retain state across calls. No outside-domain validation is required. Use only the standard library, with no real threads or network. This computes the stated finite closed model and canonical witness, not actual CPython dispatch timing, a fairness/deadline guarantee, a full runtime simulation, or a claim that increasing capacity repairs every dependency cycle.
